bandReport.notes: COLUMN-CROP CHECK ON THE GUTTER-FALLBACK PAGE. One of my four pages is on the fallback list (26; gutterFound=false, gutterWidth 10). I opened p26.png and diffed it against the c1/c2 crops: THE CROPS ARE USABLE. The split falls just right of the printed vertical rule, so c1 carries Passage-3 and item 44 whole (all three numbered assumptions and all four options) and c2 carries Passage-4 and item 45 whole. Only single-character fragments of the neighbouring column bleed in, never a word and never an option. Pages 20, 22 and 24 all detected their gutters normally (widths 31, 18, 33) and their crops are clean. --- SEAMS, BOTH CHECKED DIRECTLY ON BOTH SIDES. 18/20 (b2 to b3, both mine): item 31 completes in full at the foot of page 18 column 2 and page 20 column 1 opens cleanly at item 32, nothing straddles it. 26/28 (b3 to a band I DO NOT OWN): I opened p28.png specifically to check this. Item 45 completes in full at the foot of page 26 column 2, and page 28 opens with a fresh 'Passage - 5' heading and item 46 — it does NOT continue item 45 and it does NOT refer back to my Passage-4. So no passage of mine governs an item on page 28 and there is no context that another band must reproduce. For that band's benefit: page 28 carries Passage-5 -> item 46 and Passage-6 -> item 47, one item each, which completes the third directions block. --- A PASSAGE THAT SPANS A PAGE BREAK, INSIDE MY OWN BAND. Page 22 column 2 opens the THIRD directions block ('Directions for the following 7 (seven) items : Read the following six passages...', numbering restarting again at 'Passage - 1') and prints Passage-1 in full, but NO ITEM FOLLOWS IT ON THAT PAGE — the passage ends at the foot of the column and its items are overleaf on page 24. So page 22 yields only items 38, 39, 40, and items 41 and 42 on page 24 both open with 'the above passage' referring back to a passage printed on the PREVIOUS page. Both carry that Passage-1 text as their context, byte-identical (written once and copied, never retyped). A band cut between pages 22 and 24 would have silently produced two items whose context was unrecoverable from their own page; it happens not to be cut there, but it is the exact shape that would go wrong and is worth recording. --- FULL PASSAGE MAPPING FOR THE THIRD BLOCK (items 41-47, six passages), reconciled against the printed count: Passage-1 -> items 41 AND 42; Passage-2 -> item 43; Passage-3 -> item 44; Passage-4 -> item 45; Passage-5 -> item 46 (page 28, not mine); Passage-6 -> item 47 (page 28, not mine). Six passages over seven items, matching the '7 (seven) items' heading exactly. Within my band the only two-item passage is Passage-1; Passages 2, 3 and 4 govern one item each and will raise 'lonely-context' warnings at merge, which are correct rather than defects. The directions preamble itself is deliberately NOT in any context field. Items 32-40 are standalone numeracy/reasoning with no passage and no context. --- PRINTED / SCAN DEFECTS AND TYPOGRAPHY. (i) ITEM 37 OPTION (b): the minus sign in '(y - x)' carries a stray ink tick on its right-hand end, so at page resolution it images as something like a broken dash rather than a clean minus. I zoomed this to 600 dpi to settle it: it is a minus sign with an attached speck, confirmed by comparing it against the clean minus printed in option (c) of the same item, which is the identical expression. Transcribed as a minus. Nothing else in the item is affected. (ii) RAISED MIDDLE DOT decimals preserved as U+00B7 exactly as printed, NOT as a full stop: Q40 options (b) '39·7' and (d) '40·3'. (iii) Items 35 and 38 print ordinals as superscripts (1st, 7th, 8th, 12th, 13th January); transcribed as plain 'st'/'th' since the superscript is typographic, not mathematical. (iv) Passage-1 of block 3 prints curly SINGLE quotes around ‘Genetic Modification (GM)’ and ‘Intellectual Property Rights’; preserved as typed. Passage-4 on page 26 prints em dashes around '— the static Development Plan —'; preserved. (v) Q45 option (d) prints 'peoples’' — the apostrophe placed AFTER the s of an already-plural 'peoples' — which is unusual but is exactly what the page shows and is transcribed verbatim, not silently corrected to 'people's'. (vi) Q38 stem prints 'her parents’ marriage' with the same trailing-apostrophe plural possessive; also verbatim. (vii) No duplicate option text and no blank option anywhere in items 32-45. --- MATH. Item 37 is the only item in this band with mathematical expressions; its variables and the expressions (y - x) and (x + y) are wrapped in \( \) inline delimiters. Item 36's X, Y, Z, item 33's ratio '4 : 7' and item 34's A and B are contestant/person labels and plain prose respectively, and are deliberately left unwrapped, consistent with items 11, 29 and 30 in my other bands. questions.context: What stands in the way of the widespread and careful adoption of ‘Genetic Modification (GM)’ technology is an ‘Intellectual Property Rights’ regime that seeks to create private monopolies for such technologies. If GM technology is largely corporate driven, it seeks to maximize profits and that too in the short run. That is why corporations make major investments for herbicide-tolerant and pest-resistant crops. Such properties have only a short window, as soon enough, pests and weeds will evolve to overcome such resistance. This suits the corporations. The National Farmers Commission pointed out that priority must be given in genetic modification to the incorporation of genes that can help impart resistance to drought, salinity and other stresses.
questions.stem: Which one of the following is the most logical, rational and crucial message conveyed by the above passage ?

options.label: A
options.text: Public research institutions should take the lead in GM technology and prioritise the technology agenda.

options.label: B
options.text: Developing countries should raise this issue in WTO and ensure the abolition of Intellectual Property Rights.

options.label: C
options.text: Private corporations should not be allowed to do agribusiness in India, particularly the seed business.

options.label: D
options.text: Present Indian circumstances do not favour the cultivation of genetically modified crops.

questions.context: Most invasive species are neither terribly successful nor very harmful. Britain's invasive plants are not widespread, not spreading especially quickly, and often less of a nuisance than vigorous natives such as bracken. The arrival of new species almost always increases biological diversity in a region; in many cases, a flood of newcomers drives no native species to extinction. One reason is that invaders tend to colonise disturbed habitats like polluted lakes and post-industrial wasteland, where little else lives. They are nature's opportunists.

options.label: B
options.text: Laws against the introduction of foreign plants are unnecessary.

options.label: C
options.text: Sometimes, the campaigns against foreign plants are pointless.

options.label: D
options.text: Foreign plants should be used to increase the biodiversity of a country.

questions.context: Diarrhoeal deaths among Indian children are mostly due to food and water contamination. Use of contaminated groundwater and unsafe chemicals in agriculture, poor hygiene in storage and handling of food items to food cooked and distributed in unhygienic surroundings; there are myriad factors that need regulation and monitoring. People need to have awareness of adulteration and ways of complaining to the relevant authorities. Surveillance of food-borne diseases involves a number of government agencies and entails a good training of inspection staff. Considering the proportion of the urban population that depends on street food for its daily meals, investing in training and education of street vendors is of great significance.
questions.stem:

3. India needs to make sufficient legislation for governing food processing industry.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid ?
